description: NaFe(TeO₃)₂ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pbca space group. Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.45-2.97 Å. Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with three equivalent TeO₅ square pyramids,  an edgeedge with one FeO₆ octahedra, and  an edgeedge with one TeO₅ square pyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.97-2.10 Å. There are two inequivalent Te sites. In the first Te site, Te is bonded to five O atoms to form distorted TeO₅ square pyramids that share corners with three equivalent FeO₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent TeO₅ square pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 36-63°. There are a spread of Te-O bond distances ranging from 1.93-2.56 Å. In the second Te site, Te is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to three O atoms. There are a spread of Te-O bond distances ranging from 1.88-1.94 Å. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one Te atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to one Na, one Fe, and two equivalent Te atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na and two Te atoms to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₂Te₂ tetrahedra. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a trigonal non-coplanar geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one Te atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to one Na, two equivalent Fe, and one Te atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one Te atom.
